parts.text: State the number of participants diagnosed with AS/HFA in this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The AS/HFA participants were the only group asked to make two judgements about each
photograph. One of these judgements was about the emotion in the photograph.
Name the other judgement this group were asked to make about each photograph.

parts.text:
Identify the two ways that the revised eyes test increased the range of scores a participant
could obtain.

parts.text: Name two objects the chimpanzee helper could choose, other than the straw and the stick.

parts.label: (b)

text: In the study by Yamamoto et al., the chimpanzee helper had access to a tray containing seven
objects. Two of these objects were the straw and the stick.

parts.text: Describe the sample used in this study.

parts.text:
Describe one result about no dream recall from REM awakenings in the first half of the night
compared to the second half of the night.

text: From the study by Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the procedure after the ‘preliminary run’ until the participant pressed the 300 volt
shock level switch.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Studies in social psychology can be used to help government officials.
Suggest how the study by Milgram could be used to help a government official make the
general public follow a new public safety guideline. Your suggestion must be ethical.

text: From the study by Milgram (obedience):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one aim of this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why the procedure was standardised in this study.

text: From the study by Pepperberg (parrot learning):
Outline what is meant by the ‘cognitive approach’ in psychology. Include examples from the study
by Andrade (doodling) in your answer.
From the study by Schachter and Singer (two factors in emotion):
Describe the procedure in the Euphoria condition from immediately after the participant was
injected, until the stooge started their routine.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one example of ‘imitative verbal aggression’ said by the participants.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Identify one example of ‘imitative non-aggressive verbal response’ said by the
participants.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two friends, Arturo and Gloria, are discussing this study in terms of validity.
Arturo believes the study does have validity but Gloria believes the study does not have
validity.
Outline why you think either Arturo or Gloria is correct, using evidence from the study.

parts.text: Describe the psychology being investigated in the study by Laney et al. (false memory).

Explain whether each ethical guideline below was broken in the study by Laney et al. (false
memory):
confidentiality ______
deception ______
informed consent ______
protection from psychological harm ______
